title: Mixed String-Construction Styles for Database Queries
pattern: Mixing secure, parameterized SQL query structures with manual string concatenation in the same database access module.
why_bad: It violates safety and reliability consistency. It exposes specific paths of the application to SQL injection attacks and breaks the predictability of query parsing.
detection: Scan modules for SQL string templates, flagging any that use string formatters (`format!`) alongside standard parameterized placeholders (`?`).
counterexample: None. String concatenation of user inputs in SQL statements is a security defect. `Strong`.
fix: Standardize all queries on parameterized statements or a type-safe query builder.
source: *Kill It with Fire* by Marianne Bellotti (2021), p. 136, 527.
